title: Microsoft Teams: Channel Agent, a built-in Copilot agent for each Teams channel
summary: The briefing supports its defaults, licensing, data-access warnings and controls with Microsoft's documentation, and explicitly reports the conflicting guidance on app management and DLP. Minor corrections should complete the retention path and flag the ambiguous block/unblock example in the PowerShell reference.

claims.quote: Built-in Teams agents like Channel Agent, Facilitator, and other built-in agents available across chats, channels, and meetings are managed from the Built-In Teams agents page

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked $true changes the Teams app's allowed/blocked state.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app
claims.fix: Add to controls[1].note: 'The PowerShell reference describes -IsBlocked $true as unblocking an app; do not assume this example blocks access.' The reference also describes a $false example as unblocking, so do not substitute a different value without verified documentation.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Agent settings > auto-creation controls automatic Channel Agent creation.

claims.quote: To enable Loop components in Teams, run `Set-SPOTenant -IsLoopEnabled $true`. The change will take a short time to apply across your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies is the page for configuring Channel Agent interaction retention.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, navigate to Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies and create a retention policy with the following policy location: - Teams chats for interactions with a channel agent
claims.fix: For a static retention policy, replace the path with 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy > Choose the type of retention policy to create > Static > Choose locations to apply the policy > Teams chats'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies in sources alongside the existing feature-specific reference.

claims.claim: New-RetentionComplianceRule -Name <String> -Policy <PolicyIdParameter> -RetentionDuration <days-or-Unlimited> -RetentionComplianceAction <Keep-or-KeepAndDelete> creates a retention rule with the stated duration and action.
claims.quote: New-RetentionComplianceRule -Name InternalCompanyRule -Policy "Internal Company Policy" -RetentionDuration Unlimited -RetentionComplianceAction Keep

claims.claim: The retention rule must be added to an existing retention policy using the Policy parameter.
claims.quote: The retention rule must be added to an existing retention policy using the Policy parameter.

claims.claim: RetentionComplianceAction accepts Keep and KeepAndDelete.
claims.quote: The RetentionComplianceAction parameter specifies the retention action for the rule. Valid values are: Delete, Keep, KeepAndDelete

claims.claim: RetentionDuration accepts an integer number of days or Unlimited.
claims.quote: The RetentionDuration parameter specifies the hold duration for the retention rule. Valid values are: An integer: The hold duration in days. Unlimited: The content is held indefinitely.

claims.claim: New-RetentionComplianceRule is available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Retention policies are not valid until a retention rule is added.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies).
